text.title: Market Research TAM SAM SOM Core Rules
text.summary: 7 testable rules for a TAM/SAM/SOM artefact: bottom-up as the primary estimate, the mandatory top-down cross-check with a >2x invalidation threshold, executable SAM filters, capacity-bounded SOM, and the price and forecast-layering constraints that keep the arithmetic honest.

rule.statement: TAM MUST be computed bottom-up as (addressable unit count × realised annual price per unit), with unit count and price each carrying an independent source. The top-down analyst figure is recorded in `top_down_vs_bottom_up` as a cross-check and MUST NOT be the headline `tam.value_usd`.

rationale.source: Bottom-up market sizing (Maurya, Running Lean; a16z/Bessemer sizing guidance)

rule.rationale: A top-down figure inherits the publisher's market definition, which is broader than what you can sell; it cannot be decomposed into units you can name, so no downstream plan — pricing, quota, capacity — can be derived from it or checked against it.

rule.statement: `top_down_vs_bottom_up` MUST carry both values and their ratio. A ratio > 2x blocks sign-off until the reconciliation note names the specific differing term — unit definition, price basis, geography, or timeframe — and restates one method under the other's assumption.
rule.rationale: A >2x gap means the two methods sized two different markets; averaging them or picking the friendlier one yields a number that describes neither, and because both halves are individually cited, review passes it.

rule.statement: SAM MUST be derived from TAM by named filters (geography, segment, regulatory eligibility, language, channel reach, integration prerequisite) each with its own retained fraction and source, multiplied out. `sam.filter_logic` stating a bare percentage of TAM is rejected.
rule.rationale: A single blended percentage hides which filter is doing all the work; when one filter is later found wrong, nobody can tell whether SAM moves 5% or 5x, so the whole estimate has to be rebuilt from scratch instead of patched.

rule.statement: SOM MUST be reconciled against a capacity model over the stated period — (sales capacity × win rate × ACV) or (traffic × signup rate × paid conversion × ACV) — not stated as a share of SAM. If the implied growth exceeds the fastest named comparable in the same category, the comparable and the justification MUST appear in `som.3yr_assumption`.
rule.rationale: SOM stated as a share of SAM is unconstrained by the company's ability to acquire and serve, yet it becomes the plan number that hiring and burn are sized against; the shortfall surfaces only when the runway does.

rule.statement: The price term in the bottom-up build MUST be realised revenue per unit — net of discount and channel margin — and MUST declare its basis: ARR, ACV, or one-off. Annualising a one-off price, or using list price where a discount schedule exists, is rejected.
rule.rationale: List price × unit count overstates by exactly the average discount, and treating a one-off purchase as recurring inflates by the replacement cycle length — an order-of-magnitude error that survives review because the arithmetic is internally consistent.

rule.statement: At most ONE forecast layer may sit in any chain. Stacking a third-party market forecast × a growth assumption × a share assumption is forbidden; where more than one uncertain term is unavoidable, the artefact MUST state the low/high range rather than a point estimate.
rule.rationale: Multiplicative terms propagate relative error: three assumptions each ±30% give a range roughly 2.5x wide from low to high, which is wide enough to contain any conclusion the author wanted, so the estimate stops constraining the decision.

rule.statement: Do NOT run when (a) no unit of consumption can be named yet (no pricing hypothesis, no buyer count) — bottom-up is impossible and top-down alone is not an output; (b) the market is a created category with no existing budget line to count against — route to jtbd-switch-interview; (c) the decision is not gated on size (a size number would not change it); (d) the only available source is a single paywalled analyst summary with no unit or price breakdown.
rule.rationale: Without a unit and a price the artefact can only restate someone else's headline number with new decimals, which is the specific failure this methodology exists to block.
